paper.title: Online Learning with Switching Costs and Other Adaptive Adversaries

settings.name_in_paper: Oblivious adversary with switching costs, bandit feedback (lower bound)
unmapped: Losses are not in a fixed interval: per-round range bounded by C (|f_t(x)-f_t(x')|<=C) and per-action drift bounded by D_t (|f_t - f_{t+1}| <= D_t), allowed to grow like sqrt(log t)
Unit switching cost added to the loss whenever X_t != X_{t-1}
Policy regret against best fixed action sequence
settings.definition_quote: A stronger adversary is the \emph{oblivious adversary with switching costs}. ... he sets $f_1(x) = \ell_1(x)$, and $\forall~t\geq 2,~~~f_t(x_{1:t}) ~=~ \ell_t(x_t) + \Ind{x_t \neq x_{t-1}}$

settings.name_in_paper: Bounded memory adaptive adversary, full-information feedback (lower bound)
unmapped: Adaptive adversary with bounded memory m (loss depends only on last m+1 actions); here m=2
Bounded per-round range C and bounded drift D_t instead of fixed loss interval
Policy regret: compared with sum_t f_t(x...x)
settings.definition_quote: the bounded memory adversary must choose loss functions that satisfy, $\forall t$, $\forall x_{1:t} \in \Acal^t$, and $\forall x'_{1:t-m-1} \in \Acal^{t-m-1}$, $f_t(x_{1:t}) ~=~ f_t(x'_{1:t-m-1},x_{t-m:t})$

settings.name_in_paper: Oblivious adversary with switching costs, full-information feedback
unmapped: Per-round loss range bounded by C (interval may drift arbitrarily)

settings.name_in_paper: Oblivious adversary, bandit feedback, bounded range and drift
unmapped: Per-round loss range bounded by C and drift bounded by D_t = O(sqrt(log t)); learner uses C and D = max_t D_t (here D is a drift bound, not a delay)
settings.definition_quote: In this setting, $f_t(x_{1:t})$ simply equals $\ell_t(x_t)$. ... The player uses the fact that each $f_t$ has a range bounded by $C$. Additionally, he defines $D = \max_{t\leq T} D_t$

unmapped: Adaptive adversary with bounded memory m (known to learner)
Per-round range C and drift D_t = O(sqrt(log t)); learner uses C, D = max_t D_t
settings.definition_quote: Proving an upper bound against an adversary with a memory of size $m$, with bandit feedback, requires a more delicate reduction. As in the previous section, we assume a finite horizon $T$ and we let $D = \max_t D_t$. Let $K = |\Acal|$ be the number of actions

settings.name_in_paper: Bandits with switching costs against i.i.d. oblivious adversary
unmapped: Subgaussian defined via tail constants b, c (P(Z > EZ + a) <= b e^{-c a^2}); algorithm uses b/c
settings.definition_quote: The strategy used by this stochastic adversary is specified by a probability distribution over oblivious loss functions. The oblivious loss function for each step $t=1,2,\dots$ is the realization on an independent draw $L_t$ from this distribution.

algorithms.name: FLL on rescaled losses (Follow the Lazy Leader reduction)
Epoch-based mini-batched Hedge with randomized exploration intervals
Staged round-robin elimination (adapted from Cesa-Bianchi et al. 2013)

conditions: drift bounded by D_t = sqrt(3 log(t) + 16)

source.label: thm:lowerbound
source.quote: For any player strategy that relies on bandit feedback and for any number of rounds $T$, there exist loss functions $f_1,\dots,f_T$ that are oblivious with switching costs, with a range bounded by $C=2$, and a drift bounded by $D_t = \sqrt{3\log(t)+16}$, such that $\E[R_T] \geq \frac{1}{40}T^{2/3}$.

results.notes: Policy regret including switching costs. Construction: Gaussian random walk with shifted second arm (gap T^{-1/3}). Lemma 2 gives 1/10 T^{2/3} against the randomized adversary (unbounded drift); not recorded separately. Applies to all stronger adversaries.

conditions: drift bounded by D_t = sqrt(3 log(t) + 18)

source.label: thm:lowerboundfullinf
source.quote: For any player strategy that relies on full-information feedback and for any number of rounds $T\geq 2$, there exist loss functions $f_1,\dots,f_T$, each with a memory of size $m=2$, a range bounded by $C=2$, and a drift bounded by $D_t = \sqrt{3\log(t)+18}$, such that $\E[R_T] \geq \frac{1}{40}(T-1)^{2/3}$.

results.notes: Policy regret. Proved via reduction from bandits with switching costs.

symbols.C_range: bound on per-round range of the loss functions (including switching cost)

source.label: thm:fullUpBound
source.quote: If each of the loss functions $f_1,f_2, \ldots$ is oblivious with switching costs and has a range bounded by $C$ then the player strategy described above attains $\Ocal(C\sqrt{T})$ expected regret.

results.notes: Horizon dependence of FLL not stated explicitly; proof says 'for any T'. Drift arbitrary. Regret includes switching costs.

symbols.C_range: bound on per-round range of the loss functions

conditions: drift bounded by D_t = O(sqrt(log t))

source.label: thm:banditObliviousUpBound
source.quote: If each of the loss functions $f_1 \ldots f_T$ is oblivious with a range bounded by $C$ and a drift bounded by $D_t = \Ocal\bigl(\sqrt{\log(t)}\bigr)$ then the player strategy described above attains $\widetilde \Ocal(C\sqrt{T})$ expected regret.

results.notes: Proof gives 2(C+D) O(sqrt T). Fixed horizon; doubling trick mentioned for infinite horizon.

conditions: drift bounded by D_t = O(sqrt(log t))
tuning: number of epochs J of order T^{2/3}

source.label: thm:banditBoundedUpper
source.quote: If each of the loss functions $f_1 \ldots f_T$ is has a memory of size $m$, a range bounded by $C$, and a drift bounded by $D_t = \Ocal\bigl(\sqrt{\log(t)}\bigr)$ then the player strategy described above attains $\widetilde \Ocal(T^{2/3})$ expected regret.

results.notes: Policy regret. Explicit pre-tuning bound: 2(C+(m+1)D)(2m+1)J + 4(C+(m+1)D)(T/J)sqrt(J ln K) + CT/J + 2(m+1)CKJ.

conditions: finite action set of size K
tuning: confidence widths C_s = sqrt(112 (b/c) K/T_s ln(KS/delta))

source.quote: Consider a finite action set $\Acal=\{1\ldots K\}$. Then for each $T$ there exists a deterministic player strategy for the bandit game with i.i.d.\ oblivious adversaries and switching costs, whose regret after $T$ steps is $\mathcal{O}\bigl(\sqrt{T\log\log\log T}\bigr)$ with high probability, provided the distribution of $L_1(x)$ is sugaussian for each $x \in \Acal$.

results.notes: Proof gives, w.p. >= 1-delta, order K lnln T + mu* sqrt(T) + sqrt(KT(ln(K/delta) + lnlnln T)); K, delta dependence hidden in the theorem. Number of switches O(K log log T). Regret defined via conditional expected losses.
